verdict.headline: Stock futures edge up as investors test last week's AI sell-off
verdict.label: Sunday night: futures reopened higher after the worst week since June; S&P 500 closed Fri at 7,659.44 (-1.09%, week -1.9%), seven points under 7,666.45; Nasdaq 26,140.03 (week -4.5%); VIX ~20; 10Y ~5.085%; Brent $109.86 Fri settle; BTC ~$82,455 (+1.2% in 24h).
verdict.horizon: Monday's session through Wednesday October 21, when Tesla, Meta and Texas Instruments report
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: stock futures reopened Sunday evening with small gains. CNBC reported Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.4% and S&P 500 and Dow futures up about 0.2%, describing traders cautiously buying last week's dip in AI shares; Bloomberg reported larger gains of 0.5% and 0.9%. The cash market last closed Friday at 7,659.44 on the S&P 500, seven points below the 7,666.45 level recent reports named as the sign of selling spreading beyond AI, after the Nasdaq's 4.5% weekly fall. Over the weekend Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two supertankers hit mines and caught fire near Hormuz, and at least nine ships have been attacked around the strait since October 11. CNBC described oil as stable early Sunday, but this run could not confirm a Brent or WTI price from the reopen. Bitcoin was near $82,455, up 1.2% in 24 hours.

What it means: the first prices after the weekend point to a pause in the selling, not a reversal. A 0.2% to 0.5% futures gain would put the S&P 500 back around or just above 7,666.45, so Monday's close, not the overnight quote, decides whether Friday's break holds. The weekend tanker news had not, on the reports available, moved oil much from Friday's $109.86 settle, which matters because oil near $110 is what keeps a Fed rate rise in discussion. The evidence conflicts on size: CNBC and Bloomberg report different futures gains, and overnight moves on thin volume often fade.

What would change the picture: a Monday close back above 7,666.45 would make Friday look like an options-expiry overshoot; a second close below it with the Dow down more than 1% would show the selling spreading past AI. A Brent settle above $110 would add to inflation pressure before the October 27-28 Fed meeting, while a fall toward $104.7 would ease it. Netflix reports Tuesday; Tesla, Meta and Texas Instruments on Wednesday, with Meta's spending plans the first direct read from a large AI buyer. Conviction is low because this run could only check sources through search results and could not confirm an oil price from the reopen.
verdict.lede_short: Stock futures reopened Sunday evening a little higher, between 0.2% and 0.9% depending on the index and the source, as investors cautiously bought last week's AI sell-off. That is a pause, not a recovery: the S&P 500 closed Friday just under 7,666, and Monday's close decides whether that break holds. Oil looked stable despite weekend tanker attacks near Hormuz, and Meta's spending plans on Wednesday are the next real test for AI stocks.

supporting_data.label: CNBC reported Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.4% and S&P 500 and Dow futures up about 0.2% on Sunday evening — investors are cautiously buying last week's AI dip, but overnight gains this small often fade by the close.
Bloomberg (subscription) reported larger futures gains of 0.5% for the S&P 500 and 0.9% for the Nasdaq 100 — the two reports disagree on size but agree on direction.

The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,659.44, seven points under 7,666.45, while the Nasdaq lost 4.5% on the week and the Dow gained 0.7% — Sunday's futures gains are enough to put the index back near that line, so Monday's close decides whether the break holds.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two supertankers hit mines and caught fire near Hormuz, and at least nine ships have been attacked around the strait since October 11 — the supply risk behind Brent's $109.86 Friday settle has not eased.

Brent settled Friday at $109.86, near $110, and Iran says the strait would reopen only if US forces leave the region — a de-escalation that would bring oil down still depends on terms the US has not accepted.

Netflix reports Tuesday and Tesla, Meta and Texas Instruments on Wednesday — Meta's spending plans are the first direct read from a large AI buyer on whether the chip selling reflects a real slowdown.
Bitcoin traded near $82,455 on Sunday night, up 1.2% in 24 hours in an $80,665 to $82,470 range — it is about $2,100 above its $80,320 low and moving with, not against, the firmer futures.
